stories.headline: Congress accuses CEC of law violation over Form 6 changes, urges Supreme Court to hold him accountable
stories.deck: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh asserted that CEC Gyanesh Kumar can still redeem himself by resigning and turning approver
stories.bodyText:
The Congress on Saturday (September 26, 2026) accused Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of knowingly breaking the law and Constitutional practices by "unilaterally" changing Form 6 and called on the Supreme Court to take suo motu cognisance and hold him accountable.
In a post on X, Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said Mr. Kumar's continued tenure is an affront to the people of India and that he must resign, as suggested by Lok Sabha Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi.
Mr. Ramesh stated that late at night on Friday (September 25, 2026), a "panicked" Election Commission directed officers to organise special enrolment camps for young voters and give them "wide publicity" through social media.
Also Read: Election Commission stops physical hearings for voters, to start enrolment drive
"But the CEC himself had earlier made it virtually impossible to add young voters through a blatantly illegal and unconstitutional change to Form 6. A new mandatory section was added that asks if your parents/grandparents were in the previous SIR, creating a barrier for first-time Gen Z voters.
"The change is completely illegal. -- Violation 1: In early July 2026, the online form was stealthily changed with no official notification," the Congress leader said.
Pointing out the second violation, he said the ECI does not have the power to amend Form 6. "This power is only held by the Union Government as per the Representation Of The People Act, 1950. This is clearly a huge overreach by the Election Commission," Mr. Ramesh said.
"Violation 3: The form was changed without any amendment to the Rules that govern it under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960. That can only be done by the Union Government with proper intimation to Parliament. A statutory form, defined by the law, was unilaterally changed by the CEC Gyanesh at the instance of the rattled PM-HM duo," he added.
Mr. Ramesh claimed that, incidentally, the two election commissioners had called for this "illegal and unauthorised" change to be reversed "so young and first-time voters can register without any harassment".
"The CEC has broken not just Constitutional conventions and practices but has also knowingly broken the law as passed by Parliament. His continuation in office is an affront to the people of India.
"A confirmed law-breaker in charge of implementing laws -- what has Indian democracy degenerated into. The Supreme Court must immediately take suo motu cognisance and hold him accountable," the Congress general secretary said.
He asserted that Mr. Kumar can still redeem himself by resigning and turning approver, a suggestion by Rahul Gandhi, adding that the youth will approve this move.
Amid a row over the Election Commission adding a declaration to the form for new voters seeking to enrol in the electoral rolls and making the registration process difficult, poll panel officials said on Friday (September 25, 2026) that as many as 2.37 crore electors in the 18- 28-year age bracket were added since the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise was rolled out in Bihar last June.
After the change in the online form, it's not only the existing voters who must show details of their parents in the SIR to remain on the electoral rolls; those seeking inclusion in the voter list also have to cite details of the exercise.
By issuing instructions, the Election Commission has made it mandatory to attach SIR details of parents for new voters filling Form 6 for inclusion in the electoral rolls.
A poll panel functionary underlined that the declaration was added through instructions and that Form 6 has not been amended.
If a person fills out Form 6 online, he or she cannot proceed further till the declaration is filled.

stories.headline: Election Commission stops physical hearings for voters, to start enrolment drive
stories.deck: Days after reports of rift within EC, it announces several steps to address SIR concerns; new voters seeking inclusion in rolls after SIR need not submit declaration with Form 6; it extends deadline for filing claims and objections in Delhi and Maharashtra
stories.bodyText:
The Election Commission of India (ECI) on Saturday (September 26, 2026) announced a slew of measures addressing concerns over the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls across the country, including stopping physical hearings for unmapped voters or those with logical discrepancies in their enumeration forms.
It said that the declaration accompanying Form 6 (used for fresh voter registration) is mandatory only during the current SIR process. This in effect means that new voters who seek inclusion in electoral rolls after the ongoing SIR need not submit any such declaration.
The commission also said that any person whose name has got left out during SIR or thereafter, and any person including young/ first-time voters, may apply to the electoral registration officer (ERO) concerned, for inclusion of their names in the electoral rolls. A special drive will immediately be launched for their enrolment, it said in a press note.
The SIR process has already been completed in 20 States and Union Territories.
The fresh initiatives of the poll body came after a meeting of the full bench of the commission on Saturday afternoon (September 26, 2026) and days after reports emerged of a rift within the Election Commissioners over these and other issues in the SIR process as well as the internal working of the ECI.
The press note confirmed that the two Commissioners had written to the Cabinet Secretary but said it was not related to any policy matter of the commission or IT division but related to working of an officer on deputation to the ECI. “The work re-distribution orders issued by the concerned officer were not actually implemented after the orders of the two Commissioners,” it clarified.
The commission’s press note was pertinently accompanied by a photograph of all the three Election Commissioners and mentioned that it “has the approval of the full commission”.
As far as physical hearings were concerned, the statement said: “In case of any person to whom notice has been issued during the ongoing SIR, for being unmapped and for logical discrepancies, BLOs (booth-level officers) will visit the homes of such persons for collection of documents and thereafter upload them on the ECINet, for decision by the ERO.”
“Such persons need not be called for hearing to ERO/AERO office. Only in exceptional circumstances, as decided by the ERO, the hearing will be held preferably online. Any adult member of the family can be authorised by the elector to attend the hearing on their behalf, if required. Facilities for the online hearing are to be strengthened.”
As regards new voter registration, the EC maintained that the declaration form attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Supreme Court, but for non-SIR period, the forms appFmahalicable as per rules (the Registration of Electors Rules 1960) will be used for new voter inclusion.
Also read | Declaration part of Form 6 changed since SIR in Bihar
Access issue
The other issue that had attracted the ire of the two Election Commissioners was the supposed centralisation of management of voter rolls through the ECINet portal, with field officers unable to access it in many cases.
The statement said that “A Committee headed by Sr. Deputy Election Commissioner (DEC) and including an independent expert from IIT/IIIT will review the ECINET to double-check that it complies with the provisions of the Acts and Rules and submit report to the Commission”. It added that henceforth, all the new initiatives about IT modules and portals will be discussed in the Committee of Officers (COO) before approval by the commission.
“Field officers have role-based access to the ECINET system as per their statutory powers. In case, any further flexibility is required by the field officers, that will be made operational,” it added.
The commission also extended the period for filing claims and objections for Delhi till October 30 and for Maharashtra till October 12.
Many other administrative measures were also announced. These include circulation of an advanced agenda and issuance of minutes for all of Commission’s meetings, completion of annual performance appraisal reports of all the officers within the stipulated time frame, approval of the commission for foreign trips of officers and compliance with all directions issued by the Commissioners to the officers of the Commission.
The Opposition, which has been seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, remained unimpressed with the statement. Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said: “The CEC thinks he can hide behind protocol. He stands exposed and is now petrified as an entire country seeks to hold him accountable.”
“The ongoing SIR which has turned to be method of massive disenfranchisement of several crores of India must be suspended immediately without delay. In the meantime, nothing short of the CEC’s resignation or prosecution will suffice”.
Published - September 26, 2026 05:47 pm IST

stories.headline: 400 flights cancelled, 100,000 without power as Nor-easter hits US East Coast
stories.bodyText:
A strong nor’easter hitting the US East Coast from Washington, DC, to Maine this weekend forced airlines to cancel over 400 flights and left more than 100,000 homes and businesses without power at one point on Saturday.
Flight tracker FlightAware said 439 flights involving US airports had been cancelled and 2,459 delayed as of 6.13 pm (local time).
The governors of New York and New Jersey on Friday declared states of emergency in counties expected to see the worst of the storm, including New York City. Connecticut’s governor activated the state’s Emergency Operations Center.
More than 68,000 homes and businesses remained without power in New Jersey, Connecticut, New York and Pennsylvania as of 6.07 (local time), according to PowerOutage.com. The figure was down from more than 119,000 customers earlier in the day.
New York had more than 31,000 customers without power, while Connecticut and New Jersey each had more than 12,000.
PSEG Long Island said severe weather was affecting 13,212 electric customers across Long Island and the Rockaways as of 5 pm (local time). The company said the storm brought down trees, branches and wires, and that it had restored power to more than 45,100 customers affected since Friday morning.
Central Hudson Gas & Electric Corporation said crews were working to restore power to more than 19,000 homes and businesses in New York state as of 4 pm (local time) Parts of Ulster County were among the hardest-hit areas, and restoration efforts were expected to continue into Sunday.
Flooding was reported in parts of New Jersey, from Bergen County in the north to Cape May County in the south, NJ.com reported. Voluntary evacuations were ordered in some Jersey Shore communities. MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford also announced that rock band AC/DC’s Friday concert had been postponed until October 2.
The US National Weather Service said the nor’easter would bring coastal flooding, rip currents, strong wind gusts and heavy rain to the Mid-Atlantic and New England regions through Monday.

stories.headline: Crews thin trees at Mark Twain Lake to help 200,000 endangered Indiana bats
stories.bodyText:
Every autumn, as forests begin to thin naturally, another kind of clearing takes place around Missouri’s Mark Twain Lake. This time, the goal is not timber production or development, but making room for one of North America’s most vulnerable bats. According to a report by WGEM, about 200,000 endangered Indiana bats spend the warmer months in the forests surrounding the lake before heading east to hibernate at Sodalis Nature Preserve near Hannibal. That represents roughly one-third of the species’ entire North American population, making the landscape an unusually important stronghold for the bats.
Opening up the forest
The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, working with The Conservation Fund, has begun forest stand improvement work across public wildlife management areas around Mark Twain Lake. The project focuses on reopening flight and foraging corridors that have become increasingly crowded after decades without active timber management, states the online report.
For more than 40 years, shade-tolerant trees such as sugar maple and ironwood have filled in the forest’s middle canopy. While these trees are part of a healthy woodland, their dense growth can block sunlight and create obstacles for bats moving between feeding areas and roost trees, states the report.
Rather than clearing large sections of forest, crews are using a targeted technique known as hack and squirt. Workers make small cuts around the trunks of selected trees and apply herbicide directly into those openings. The method allows crews to remove specific trees while leaving the surrounding forest largely intact.
Dead trees become bat habitat
One of the unusual benefits of the approach comes after the targeted trees die. They are left standing, gradually becoming snags that can remain part of the ecosystem for years. Indiana bats rely on cracks, crevices and peeling bark in mature trees for roosting, particularly in the overstory oaks found throughout the area. Depending on the tree, a treated snag can provide useful habitat for roughly four to 10 years before naturally breaking down.
As per the report, treatments are carried out in late summer and early autumn, when trees begin moving nutrients and stored energy toward their roots in preparation for winter. That movement helps carry the herbicide deeper into the trees.
More than a bat project
Opening the middle layer of the forest is expected to benefit more than Indiana bats. With fewer trees blocking the canopy, additional sunlight can reach the forest floor, encouraging native grasses, flowering plants and young oak-hickory growth. Those changes can improve habitat for deer, wild turkey and other wildlife that depend on the forest understory.
An initial 30-acre phase was completed last year, and crews are now working toward treating more than 250 acres around Mark Twain Lake by November 1. The wildlife management areas remain open to hikers, hunters and other visitors during the work. Visitors are being asked to give forestry crews room to operate as the habitat restoration continues.

stories.headline: Boeing flags 737 MAX software glitch affecting landing navigation feature: Report
stories.bodyText: Boeing has identified a previously undisclosed 737 MAX software glitch that could cause an automated navigation feature to fail during landing, the Wall Street Journal reported on Saturday, citing company documents.The issue emerged from a cockpit software update and can occur when flight crews alter their planned flight path after a missed approach, the report said.When reached for comment, Boeing said it informed all 737 operators last month about the software issue under which pilots may not have access to automated flight guidance during a specific landing scenario..Delhi-bound IndiGo Boeing 787 faces technical issue, returns to London."We shared information with operators that reinforced existing pilot procedures for safely handling such cases. Our engineers are working on a software update to permanently address the issue," Boeing said in an emailed statement to Reuters.The Federal Aviation Administration said it was aware of a potential issue in a software update for the flight computers on certain Boeing 737 MAX airplanes and was working closely with Boeing and the airlines."The FAA will convene a Corrective Action Review Board and will take immediate action if it identifies a safety concern," the FAA said in a statement.Boeing has been under intense regulatory and safety scrutiny in recent years following two fatal 737 MAX crashes in 2018 and 2019 that led to a worldwide grounding of the aircraft, and after a mid-air cabin panel blowout on a nearly new Alaska Airlines MAX 9.Southwest Airlines and United Airlines have asked Boeing not to deliver new 737 MAX aircraft equipped with the affected software and instead requested an earlier version, according to WSJ.It was not immediately clear how many aircraft are operating with the flawed software, the report said. Boeing, airlines and regulators are assessing the issue and whether it poses a flight-safety concern, it added.

briefs.headline: ECI’s ‘unanimous clarification’ on SIR puts to rest all misconceptions: says A.P. CM Naidu
briefs.deck: Attempts to undermine global confidence in India’s democratic framework or electoral processes for short-term political gain are deeply unfortunate, he says
briefs.bodyText:
Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has stated that the unanimous clarification issued by the Election Commission, led by Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, alongside Election Commissioners S.S. Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, on Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls reaffirmed the integrity and credibility of India’s constitutional bodies and put to rest all the misconceptions surrounding the process.
The decisions concerning the SIR were taken collectively and in strict adherence to established institutional protocols, Mr. Naidu observed in a social media post on Saturday (September 26, 2026).
Also Read: Election Commission stops physical hearings for voters, to start enrolment drive
Mr. Naidu noted that attempts to undermine global confidence in India’s democratic framework or electoral processes for short-term political gain were “deeply unfortunate.”
“Electoral outcomes reflect the people’s mandate and in a robust democracy, leadership also means accepting both victories and defeats with grace and humility,” he commented, adding that it was the collective responsibility of leaders across party lines to uphold public confidence in India’s democratic process.

briefs.headline: In Bihar, criminal escapes police custody by jumping into river
briefs.deck: According to police, there has been no trace of the criminal since he jumped into the river. Police teams are conducting raids at all his possible hideouts.
briefs.bodyText:
In a bizarre incident in Bihar’s Bhagalpur district, a criminal detained under the Arms Act escaped police custody by jumping into a river. The incident took place on Saturday (September 26, 2026) afternoon in the Jagdishpur Police Station area.
According to police, they got a tip-off from an informer that a criminal against whom many other cases were lodged was seen near Saidpur Ghat at the bank of the Chandan River carrying a country-made musket and cartridges.
A police team rushed to the spot to apprehend the criminal identified as Santosh Yadav, a resident of Motidah village. Police reached the spot in time and took him into custody.
The police team, comprising four constables, were escorting him to the jeep, however they had to cross a bamboo bridge of nearly 50 meters. While walking, two constables lifted the sticks to maintain balance on the bridge.
However, when they reached near the bridge, all stopped for a few seconds, and some argument took place; then they started moving ahead again. As soon as they all reached the middle of the bridge, the criminal pulled one constable along with him and jumped into the river.
For a few minutes, both the constable and criminal began to drift rapidly with the river’s current, as most of the rivers in Bihar are in spate due to incessant rain.
Somehow, the constable managed to swim to the other side of the bank and saved his life, while the criminal, Santosh Yadav, was not found and remained missing. Bhagalpur Police expressed apprehension that after jumping in the river, the criminal must have reached the opposite bank and fled from there.
Station House Officer Ramchandra Singh said that there has been no trace of the criminal since he jumped into the river. Police teams are conducting raids at all his possible hideouts.
The family member of the criminal said that he may have drowned in the river. One family member said that he was a tractor driver and used to support the family financially.
Later, police called a team of divers and the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) to search for the criminal, but he remained untraceable till filing of this report.
Published - September 27, 2026 07:05 am IST

briefs.headline: It's not BRICS or UN, BRICS is supportive of UN: Jaishankar
briefs.deck: The External Affairs Minister says smaller groupings are supportive of UN and will push for its reform
briefs.bodyText:
External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar has said that choosing between groupings such as BRICS and the United Nations is “a false choice”, emphasising that smaller groups are supportive of the global organisation and would like to see it reformed.
Also Read: At UNGA, Jaishankar hits back at Pakistan PM on terrorism, Indus Waters Treaty
“…I think it's a false choice. The UN is the UN. It may have many shortcomings. It also has many achievements, and obviously, when you want to reform it, when you want to change it, it's natural to focus on the shortcomings. But I don't think that should lead us to be dismissive of the UN,” Mr. Jaishankar said.
The Minister was addressing a session titled ‘Ruptures & Ramparts: Building Bridges for a Changing World’ organised on the margins of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly by the Observer Research Foundation (ORF), Reliance Foundation, UN in India and the Permanent Mission of India to the UN in New York on Thursday (September 24, 2026).
Participating in the session, moderated by ORF president Samir Saran, were Jamaica’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade Kamina Johnson Smith, Suriname Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Business and Cooperation Melvin Bouva, Ghana’s Minister for Foreign Affairs Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa and President and Chief Executive of the East-West Center Celeste Connors.
Mr. Jaishankar said the UN has served the world in very significant ways. “At the end of the day, if there wasn't a UN, we'd all be sitting here trying to invent one,” he said, adding that the BRICS or other groups as well, are “coming together” of countries who have a certain viewpoint, interest or outlook and are comfortable making that combination.
Referring to the BRICS Leaders’ Summit that India hosted on September 12-13, the External Affairs Minister said: “One of the points in the BRICS is that the UN is central to the international system.” “So it's not BRICS or the UN. The BRICS is supportive of the UN, and a large part of the BRICS would like to reform the UN, some more than others,” Mr. Jaishankar said.
The BRICS grouping includes Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Indonesia, Iran, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa and the United Arab Emirates. Mr. Jaishankar said the issues highlighted by BRICS — resilience, sustainability, innovation, cooperation – are the key issues today.
“They are equally issues for the United Nations," he said. "When we sit here at the high-level week in New York, a few kilometres away from the UN headquarters, I would look at it like what did the BRICS do to strengthen the UN and strengthen the cause of UN reform. I think it nudged it a little bit stronger. It indicated a certain pressure from bottom up.”
He also noted that one gets “very interesting press” about the BRICS, without naming any publication or elaborating on the details. “If you follow the BRICS, most of the time the 'mainstream press' is very dismissive of the BRICS until the BRICS meets. Then they get a bit worked up about it.”
He said the “true test” of the BRICS was when the expansion of the grouping happened to include more countries from the original Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa. “We doubled our numbers, but believe me, we could have easily gone up four or five times. There was a huge demand from countries,” Mr. Jaishankar said, attributing this to BRICS providing a platform for “alternative thinking.
BRICS, at the end of the day, is a non-Western platform and not all members of it are post-colonial societies and span multiple continents, he said.
“The other, in that sense, is the G7.. But what brings them (BRICS) together is really the sense that there are strong non-Western viewpoints, contributions and beliefs which need to be taken into account, and the non-Western segment of the global debate is growing in weight, and that is why the BRICS is getting more significant,” the Minister said.
Asked to choose between interest, trust or value, Mr. Jaishankar said he would probably try to get the best out of all three.
“Interest is a common-sense term. But I do believe that the word trust, in a way, has — I don't want to say replaced value — become a more dominant concept in diplomacy,” said Mr. Jaishankar, stressing that “values are often preached and not practised” but trust is earned.
“Trust is record-based. It is empirical. If you've done something good, something you know contributive, people remember it. If you have behaved badly, people remember that too,” he said. “So, I put a lot of credence on trust because, to me, trust is an empirical concept derived from experience. It reflects the real feelings of the world, and it's a very democratic term. You don't have to be big to be trusted. You can be trusted if you're small. You've got to be good or decent to be trusted,” Mr. Jaishankar added.
Published - September 26, 2026 10:53 pm IST

briefs.headline: Asian Games 2026 India’s medallists: Full list of winners
briefs.deck: Here’s the full list of Indian medallists at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026 categorised by sport
briefs.bodyText:
The 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games are underway in Japan. India is currently placed at the 10th spot on the medals’ table with 30 medals. China is leading the table with 176 medals. Japan is second with 129 medals and Republic of Korea is third with 73 medals.
On Saturday (September 26, 2026), India’s Sawan Barwal won a silver medal in the men’s marathon. India’s women’s kabaddi team extended their dominance at the Asian Games securing yet another gold medal after a thrilling 37-34 win over Iran in the finals. The men’s hockey team continued it’s winning streak, defeating Japan by 2-0, securing the semifinal berth in the big-ticket sports event.
Simultaneously, the squash squad led by teen-sensation Anahat Singh and Abhay Shetty in singles category stormed into the final game. The duo will be competing for a gold medal in their final game on Sunday.
Women’s 50m rifle 3P team comprising of Vidarsa Vinod, Ashi Chouksey, Tilottama Sen won the silver medal. Mixed squash doubles team including Joshana Chinappa, Velavan Senthilkumar clinched the bronze medal.
On Friday (September 25, 2026), the duo of Manush Shah and Diya Chitale secured a historic bronze medal in table tennis mixed doubles after stunning the world No. 4 pair from Hong Kong to enter the semi-finals.
Baranica Elangovan entered her name in the record books by winning a historic bronze medal for India in the women’s pole vault event at the Asian Games
Indian long-distance runner Gulveer Singh upgraded his Asian Games medal from bronze to silver in the men’s 10,000m.
India’s Manpreet Kaur clinched the bronze medal in women’s shot put competition of the Asian Games with an effort of 17.17m in Nagoya on Friday (September 25, 2026).
Kamaljeet and Suruchi Singh won gold in the mixed team 10m air pistol event. The Indian team, comprising Aishwary Pratap Singh Tomar, Rudranksh Patil and Niraj Kumar, won silver in the men’s 50m rifle 3P team event.
The Indian 4x400m mixed relay quartet of Vishal T.K., M.R. Poovamma, Manu T.S. and Vithya Ramraj earned a silver medal in the final at the Paloma Mizuho Stadium.
Manpreet Kaur clinched a bronze medal in the Women’s Shot Put final with a season-best throw of 17.17 meters.
The duo of Manush Shah and Diya Chitale secured a historic bronze in Table Tennis Mixed Doubles after stunning the world No. 4 pair from Hong Kong to enter the semi-finals.
Seema Kumari, competing in her first Asiad, won a bronze medal in the 10,000m at the Asian Games, 16 years after Preeja Sreedharan and Kavita Raut’s historic gold-silver double in 2010.
Manipur’s Naorem Roshibina Devi won her third consecutive Asian Games medal, clinching silver after losing to Zhang Xiaoyu in the women’s 60kg wushu final on Thursday (September 24, 2026).
Jay Meena secured India’s first-ever soft tennis medal at the Asian Games, fetching a bronze after losing to Japan’s Takuya Kurosaka in the men’s singles semifinals. Star Indian weightlifter Mirabai Chanu completed her medal collection, winning a silver medal in the women’s 49kg event in the Asian Games.
Lakshya Sen and Ayush Shetty faltered against higher-ranked opponents as the Indian men’s team concluded with a bronze medal after losing 1-3 to their rivals, China, in the semifinals.
The Indian Women’s Cricket Team clinched a historic victory at the Karogi Athletic Park in Nisshin, Aichi. Facing off against Sri Lanka in a high-stakes final, the Women in Blue triumphed to secure India’s very first gold medal of the tournament.
Meanwhile, shooters have led the charge for India. The women’s skeet team, comprising Raiza Dhillon, Maheshwari Chauhan and Parinaaz Dhaliwal, won a bronze with a combined score of 331 here on September 23, 2026.
Experienced rifle shooter Elavenil Valarivan played a starring role in the country’s double-silver haul in the women’s 10m air rifle competition. Elavenil, one of India’s most accomplished rifle shooters, helped the country secure silver in the team event along with Sonam Maskar and Vidarsa Vinod. She then went on to add an individual silver.
For the men’s side, teenager Himanshu Dhillon produced a superb performance to win silver, while former world champion Rudrankksh Patil clinched bronze as India secured two individual podium finishes in the men’s 10m air rifle event. The two then teamed up with Parth Mane to win another silver in the team event, finishing just behind China.
After an impressive start in shooting, India also managed to script history in Mixed Martial Arts (MMA), with Suchika Tariyal winning the nation’s first-ever bronze medal for MMA at the Asian Games.
A contingent of 501 Indian athletes, comprising 267 men and 234 women, is competing across 36 disciplines in the 2026 edition. Apart from shooting, athletics and archery too are expected to add to the medal tally. India is also defending both the men’s and women’s titles in cricket and kabaddi.

briefs.headline: A ‘superior’ CEC renders Election Commissioners ‘non-functional’, Supreme Court had warned
briefs.deck: Judgement stressed collegial functioning of poll panel and said ECs must have a say in decision-making
briefs.bodyText:
Nearly four decades ago, the Supreme Court had warned that if a Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) functions in a way that he considers himself superior and his word final, the Election Commissioners (ECs) would be rendered “non-functional or ornamental”.
The court had held that leaving the “exclusive and uncontrolled” powers of the Election Commission of India (ECI) in the hands of one person would violate democratic rule.

briefs.headline: After meeting, EC says officials will visit homes of those sent notices
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: A full meeting of the Election Commission of India on Saturday - the first after reports of alleged internal differences - decided to exempt electors who have got notices for being unmapped to the last SIR or over logical discrepancies, from hearings by electoral registration officer (ERO) or assistant EROs. Instead, EROs and AEROs will visit homes of such electors to collect documents that would then be uploaded to ECINet for a final decision by the ERO.
Bharti Jain is senior editor with The Times of India, New Delhi. She has been writing on security matters since 1996. Having covered the Union home ministry, security agencies, Election Commission and the ‘prime’ political beat, the Congress, for The Economic Times all these years, she moved to TOI in August 2012. Her repertoire of news stories delves into the whole gamut of issues related to terrorism and internal strife, besides probing strategic affairs in India’s neighbourhood.

briefs.headline: Iran insists on diplomatic solution after Trump rejects peace plan
briefs.bodyText: Iran on Sunday insisted that only diplomacy can solve its conflict with the United States and Israel after US President Donald Trump said he rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end fighting."Our conditions are clear, and any move toward reopening the Strait of Hormuz is contingent on these conditions being met," Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi posted on social media. "Only a negotiated solution can get them out of this deadlock."Iran announced a peace proposal earlier this week at the UN General Assembly in New York, saying it had been transmitted to the Americans via Qatari mediators. Trump on Saturday said he rejected the plan and argued that desperation drives the Iranians’ push for an agreement on the key waterway."They want to make a deal to open the Hormuz Strait immediately because they're losing so badly," Trump told reporters at the White House.Despite Trump's public statements, mediators facilitating US-Iran talks with the United States have not officially relayed a US rejection of the plan, according to Araqchi..Trump rejects Iran's seven-day ceasefire plan, expects renewed bombing after midterms: Report."We are waiting for the mediators to convey the definitive views to us, and we will make a decision based on them," Araqchi posted.The US has imposed an economic blockade on Iran to put pressure on Tehran to stop Iranian attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, which have drastically reduced shipping through the area even as Trump repeatedly asserts that the US controls the waterway.The Wall Street Journal first reported that Trump had rejected the Iranian proposal, citing unnamed US officials.It said Trump was privately skeptical that Iran would meet his demands and had told his staff that he sees a renewed bombing campaign as likely after the November US midterm elections.A US official had said earlier that discussions with Iran through mediators were "positive and constructive".Conflict has disrupted oil flows, harmed global economyThe Iranians also engaged their Saudi rivals regarding the Strait of Hormuz, underscoring the stakes of a seven-month-old conflict that has disrupted oil flows through a critical shipping lane and taken a toll on the global economy.Araqchi told reporters at the United Nations on Friday the proposed deal would trigger a seven-day countdown to reopening the strait and a pause in regional fighting."If there is seriousness on the US side to come to a deal and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, everything is now prepared," Araqchi said. If the US were to agree, the warring parties could start wider talks "on mutually agreed subjects."That could potentially include discussions of Iran's nuclear program. Trump has said Tehran must never acquire a nuclear bomb, while a senior Iranian official told Reuters that Iran would show no flexibility over its nuclear program even if the US accepted its peace deal..'We do not wish to continue': Iran's president says it is up to US to choose if it wants to end Iran war.Iran would grant no concessions over its rights, includingenriching uranium or shipping its highly enriched uranium out of the country, the official said.Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, in an interview with the CBS show "Face the Nation", said Tehran was ready for talks on its nuclear program and other issues, but would not accept "bullying or coercion"."Iran is not seeking war, but will defend itself against pressure, threats and attacks,” Pezeshkian said, adding that it had already agreed that "we're not supposed to develop nuclear weapons".Previous attempts at diplomacy have failed to end the war, which began on February 28 with US and Israeli attacks.Since then the war has alternated between pauses and renewed strikes, killing thousands while degrading Iran's conventional forces and damaging Iran's already ailing economy.Iran and its allies have retaliated by extending the conflict throughout the region. Iran has struck US allies in the Gulf with drones and missiles while its Houthi allies in Yemen have targeted Saudi interests.

stories.headline: AI hits wrong tune, mistakes guitar for helmetless pillion in Bengaluru
stories.deck: When Souvik Dutta received an automated fine in Bengaluru for a helmet violation while riding with a guitar, he took to social media to voice his concerns. The joint commissioner responded, promising to look into the matter. This incident sheds light on the ongoing issues with AI-based traffic surveillance, prompting police to re-evaluate automatically generated fines through manual verification…
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: When world-renowned violinist Philippe Quint accidentally left a 300-year-old, multi-million-dollar Stradivarius at the back of a New York City cab, the driver thought it was a forgotten gym bag. But Bengaluru’s AI-equipped traffic cameras have taken confusion over an inanimate object to a whole new level, with something as harmless as a guitar landing on the wrong side of the city’s traffic law.
Souvik Dutta was riding his wife’s scooter in the city, with his guitar strapped to his back. However, the traffic surveillance system appeared to have seen something else: An unhelmeted pillion rider!
Challan wrong? Here's how to challenge it
Dutta said he was slapped with a Rs 500 penalty for “pillion not wearing protective head gear”. One of the AI cameras installed on Outer Ring Road had captured him at noon on Sept 15. The challan, along with “photographic evidence”, was generated the next day.
Taking to social media, Dutta appealed to Bengaluru traffic police to revoke the challan. His post, accompanied by the challan details, took a swipe at the city’s AI-based traffic enforcement system: “So much for AI-based traffic violation detection!” the post read.
When
 TOI
 brought the matter to the notice of joint commissioner of police (traffic) Karthik Reddy, he said he would look into the issue. “If found true, we will revoke the violation,” he assured.
Bengaluru traffic police had adopted an AI-based surveillance system in Dec 2022 and run it without any human validation at the backend. However, when complaints pertaining to vehicle-number plates being wrongly read started cropping up, police decided to manually validate all violations raised by AI.
In another incident in Belagavi district’s Athani, a car owner was reportedly issued a Rs 500 fine for “not wearing a helmet” after an AI camera captured his car. The owner responded by making a video of himself driving the car with a helmet on!
According to online chatter, two years ago, a motorist was fined for not wearing a seat belt even though he claimed he was strapped in. Reality: The seat belt was difficult for the system to distinguish from the driver’s shirt colour.
And the problem is not unique to Bengaluru or any Indian city. According to media reports in May this year, about 3,000 drivers in Western Australia had appealed camera-detected seat belt infringements, with 60% of those appeals succeeding.
How to challenge a traffic challan
* File a dispute online: Visit 
https://btp.karnataka.gov.in
 or use the official BTP ASTraM / KSP mobile app
* Select the issue: Choose the ‘Problem in Challan’ or ‘Raise a Dispute’ option, enter your vehicle details, and describe the error
* Attach proof: Upload images or documents supporting your claim and submit the form
* Alternative: You can email your dispute with your vehicle number and photo evidence to 
automationpubbcp@ksp.gov.in
 or 
bangloretrafficpolice@gmail.com
* Follow-up: BTP representatives typically acknowledge grievances within 48 hrs. If unresolved, proceed to a virtual or physical magisterial court

stories.headline: Man shoots puppy with air gun in Karnataka, then apologises
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru: A five-month-old puppy sustained injuries on its neck after a local resident shot and injured it with his air gun in Madanayakanahalli near Nelamangala recently. A petition was filed at the jurisdictional Madanayakahalli police station against the man identified as S Krishnamurthy, 65, of Kanva Layout.
Later, he apologised for his act, stating he had shot towards a pack of stray dogs, fearing they could hurt his livestock, police said.
According to police, the incident took place on Sept 20 when pet lovers Sindhu, Sahana and others saw Krishnamurthy holding the air gun near a site where they usually fed the dogs. At the same time, they noticed blood oozing from the puppy.
“On the same stretch lived Krishnamurthy. He had livestock including chicken, sheep and goat in his backyard. Saying stray dogs will attack them, he had erected a fence,” an investigating officer said.
“That day, I saw a pack of dogs near the fence and feared that they would somehow break in and harm my stock. That’s why I randomly shot at them from a distance, with an intention of frightening them,” Krishnamurthy told cops.
Meanwhile, the complainants immediately shifted the bleeding puppy into an auto before taking it to a veterinary hospital. There were heated arguments between the complainants and Krishnamurthy when the former questioned him.

stories.headline: AI camera mistakes guitar for pillion rider in Bengaluru, issues fine for not wearing helmet
stories.deck: After getting a ₹500 challan, the rider complains to the Bengaluru Traffic Police and seeks rectification; the incident draws attention to the limitations of AI-dependent traffic systems; AI sharpens with more data, says a senior official
stories.bodyText:
An artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled enforcement traffic camera, installed to detect traffic violations in Bengaluru, recently issued a routine helmet violation challan to a not-so-routine defaulter: a guitar case riding on its owner’s back.
Souvik Dutta was travelling on his scooter from Hebbal towards Tin Factory with a guitar strapped to his back. The AI camera apparently mistook the guitar case for a pillion rider and wrongly identified it as a person travelling without a helmet. A challan, along with a photograph captured by the camera, was subsequently sent to Mr. Dutta’s wife who owns the scooter.
He raised a complaint on the Bengaluru Traffic Police’s (BTP) official handle, stating, “I was riding my wife’s two-wheeler alone with my guitar slung on my back in Bangalore. @blrcitytraffic, my wife received a traffic challan (notice no. 86202541) for ‘pillion riding without helmet’. So much for AI-based traffic violation detection! Pls revoke the challan.”
Responding to his post, BTP officials asked him to contact the traffic automation section for rectification of violations.
Limitations of AI monitoring
The incident has drawn attention to the limitations of automated traffic enforcement systems. Many motorists, taking to social media, raised concerns that the enforcement cameras book them for violations for jumping a signal even if they cross the zebra crossing a little to allow other vehicles that have a green signal to pass through.
A senior traffic police officer admitted that the reported pillion rider violation was a false flag, caused by an error in judgment by the artificial intelligence system, which happens occasionally. Sometimes, it even flags a small child sitting between two people on a scooter for pillion riding without a helmet, he said. Such violations can be questioned, he said, following which they are verified and rectified.
“The AI system sharpens with more and continuous data feeding, and it can go wrong occasionally. We already have a team that usually verifies such wrong flaggings and updates them. This might be one of the oversights, and we will rectify it,” he said, admitting that the system has yet to achieve 100% accuracy.

stories.headline: Property tax revision cases rise to 37,216 in Bengaluru
stories.deck: A corporation commissioner explains that revision cases and unassessed properties are being identified stringently, considering that property tax is one of the major sources of income for the new corporations
stories.bodyText:
The Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) has revised the property tax in 13,253 cases during the current financial year up to August-end.
According to GBA documents accessed by The Hindu, at the end of the previous financial year, 23,963 cases had been identified. With the new additions, the total number of cases being revised stands at 37,216.
The GBA had earlier sent notices to over 23,000 properties for declaring incorrect property details. Enforcement has been tightened as the new corporations explore options to expand their revenue base, while they have failed to unlock diverse revenue avenues.
Of the 23,963 cases identified last year, the GBA was to collect ₹190.92 crore. However, so far, a meagre ₹12.32 crore from 4,960 cases has been collected.
According to the latest report, Bengaluru West accounted for the highest recovery at ₹4.16 crore from 1,488 revision cases, followed by Bengaluru Central at ₹2.93 crore from 640 cases, Bengaluru South at ₹2.53 crore from 1,127 cases, Bengaluru North at ₹1.47 crore from 1,152 cases, and Bengaluru East at ₹1.23 crore from 553 cases.
Bengaluru West had the highest number of revision cases at 12,820, involving ₹203.20 crore, followed by Bengaluru South with 8,773 cases involving ₹151.49 crore, and Bengaluru North with 6,913 cases involving ₹67.03 crore. Bengaluru Central had 5,533 cases involving ₹82.75 crore, while Bengaluru East had 3,177 cases involving ₹49.94 crore.
Strengthening revenue sources
A corporation commissioner explained that revision cases and unassessed properties were being identified stringently, considering that property tax is one of the major sources of income for the new corporations.
“On the basis of the Revenue Department’s drone survey, field verification was done to filter out the incorrect flaggings in the last financial year. Now, even GPS is being used to verify,” he said.
Earlier this year, there were claims that the GBA relied only on the drone survey to revise property tax cases, but the authority clarified that field verifications were being carried out.
Unassessed properties brought under tax net
Meanwhile, the five city corporations have added 18,095 unassessed properties to the property tax net during the current financial year, collecting ₹31.63 crore from them.
Bengaluru East accounted for the largest number of such properties, with 7,004 properties and ₹12.35 crore collected. Bengaluru West followed with 4,027 properties and ₹10.37 crore, while Bengaluru South added 3,354 properties and collected ₹2.65 crore.
Bengaluru North added 3,031 properties and collected ₹1.76 crore, while Bengaluru Central added 679 properties and collected ₹4.51 crore. By August-end, the corporations had added 1,414 unassessed properties.

briefs.headline: Thief sneaks into paying guest accommodation in Bengaluru, escapes with 12 phones & 7 laptops
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 While residents slept through the night, a thief allegedly broke into a paying guest (PG) accommodation in Chikkabegur and fled with 12 mobile phones and seven laptops, leaving 11 inmates to discover the theft only the next morning.
The intruder reportedly took advantage of several unlocked room doors in the multi-storey building before escaping with the valuables.
Lenin, 20, a student staying at Sri Venkateshwara Luxury Co-live PG, told police that he went to bed around 11 pm on Sept 22. When he woke up at around 5.30 am the next day, he found that his mobile phone was missing.
A subsequent search of his room and neighbouring rooms revealed that several other devices belonging to his friends and fellow inmates were also missing. The stolen items included a MacBook, laptops, smartphones and an iPhone. The valuables belonged to 11 inmates.
The inmates also reported that other valuables were missing. Soon after the theft came to light, they informed the PG management and checked the CCTV footage before approaching the police.
A police officer said the thief, dressed as a software engineer and carrying a bag, sneaked into the building during the night. 
A small gate is kept open at night to allow inmates returning from work to enter after their duty hours. The building has no security guard, while the person in charge was asleep in his room.
The thief allegedly moved from room to room during the intervening hours and, fortunately for him, found that several doors had been left unlocked from inside. He put the laptops and mobile phones into his bag, made his way to the ground floor and escaped.
After being alerted about the burglary, Begur police rushed to the spot and examined the CCTV footage. Police said the camera was of poor quality and failed to capture the thief’s face clearly. However, cameras installed in neighbouring buildings provided clues that he was heading towards Tamil Nadu. With the help of technical analysis, police tracked his movements.
A police team was deployed to trace him. Initially, police suspected that he would head towards Hosur or Krishnagiri and followed that route. However, the thief, who was travelling by bus, continued to Chennai.
The police team also reached Chennai and, with the assistance of local police, searched a market near Marina Beach. However, the thief managed to disappear into the crowded marketplace.
Local police later informed the Begur team that the stolen laptops and mobile phones could have been dismantled and sold as spare parts in the market, which has more than 1,000 shops, making recovery of the valuables difficult.
A case has been registered under Section 305 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
Police have instructed the PG owner to install high-quality CCTV cameras and biometric access systems if employing a security guard is not financially feasible.

briefs.headline: Illustrators take centre stage at children’s literature fest in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Times News Network
Bengaluru: Illustrators are no longer just the people behind the pictures. With picture books, comics and graphic novels gaining traction in India, illustrators are increasingly being recognised as storytellers in their own right. The shift was evident at the ongoing Neev Lit Fest 2026 at Neev Academy, Yamalur, where illustrators were celebrated alongside authors.
“It is the best time to be an illustrator. Graphic novels have made a serious arrival in India. The quantity is not yet there, but the quality is extremely good,” said Kavitha Gupta Sabarwal, co-founder, NLF. She, however, pointed to the high production costs involved in graphic novels and picture books, particularly when creators choose not to use AI-generated art.
India is also seeing a surge in picture books, but the genre faces challenges ranging from production costs to perceptions about the value of visual storytelling. Unlike in several other countries, where writers often illustrate their own books, Indian publishing largely continues to separate the roles of writer and illustrator.
“Ten years ago, the illustrator was always treated as someone who creates some drawings. 
Today, people see the value in illustrations. But it is still not enough,” Kavita said.
Graphic novelist Charbak Dipta said comics in India are still in a “blossoming state”, with growing interest among both children and adults. “The common perception is that comics are for children. But it is a very powerful medium of storytelling,” he said.
Dipta also called for greater institutional support, including a national comic award, saying it could encourage creators and give the medium greater recognition.
The growing demand for visual storytelling comes amid another debate — the role of AI in illustration. Author-illustrator Angie Kand said AI-generated imagery strips away the human process behind art.
“The beautiful part of making art is trying to process something through your own understanding and lived experiences. AI strips all of that away,” she said.
Illustrators at the festival said they do not use AI in their work, arguing that doing so would take away the creative process that makes illustration rewarding.
For publishers, however, economics remains a major hurdle. Duckbill Books co-founder Anushka Ravishankar said rising input costs, including the impact of GST on materials and services used in book production, have pushed up prices.
“Books are exempt from GST, and we could not get input credit. So we were hit from both sides and had to increase prices,” she said.
Anushka also pointed to a deeper cultural challenge — the tendency to value words over visual art. “There is this notion that words are more respectable than pictures. Therefore, it has been hard to get picture books to have the importance they need to have,” she said.
Yet, she argued, picture books remain crucial to developing a reading culture among children. “For a child getting into reading, you have to start with the picture book because that is when they learn to love the printed page and the whole process of reading,” she said.
The economics also affects illustrators, who, Anushka said, remain underpaid. One possible model, she suggested, is royalty-sharing, though that shifts some of the commercial risk to illustrators if a book does not sell.

briefs.headline: Dakshina Kannada Congress to hold protest against ECI in Mangaluru on Sept 28
briefs.deck: Protest march to begin at Pumpwell Circle at 10.30am; district chief seeks CEC’s resignation, high-level probe
briefs.bodyText:
Mangaluru: Dakshina Kannada District Congress Committee (DKCC) will hold a protest rally in the city Monday against “partisan conduct” of the 
Election Commission of India
 (ECI), DKCC president Padmaraj R Poojary said Saturday.
Addressing a press conference, Poojary alleged that chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar had undermined democratic institutions by favouring one political party and disregarding objections raised by election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.
“The ECI is the foundation of democracy and must safeguard the principle of one person, one vote,” Poojary said, claiming the two commissioners had raised 14 objections. He demanded Kumar’s resignation and sought a high-level inquiry by the central govt.
The protest march will begin at 10.30am from Mahaveer (Pumpwell) Circle and proceed for around 2km before culminating at the deputy commissioner’s office. Poojary said more than 1,000 Congress workers and citizens are expected to participate.
Referring to leader of opposition in Lok Sabha, 
Rahul Gandhi
, Poojary said that allegations concerning “vote chori” in elections in Maharashtra and Karnataka’s Mahadevapura constituency, Poojary said questions had also been raised about recent electoral outcomes in Bihar and West Bengal.
Poojary also criticised former Mysuru MP Pratap Simha over his remarks on the state govt’s recognition of Tulu as the second official language. He said the move represented the cultural identity and pride of Tulunadu.
“By asking what financial benefit the recognition would bring, Simha has hurt the sentiments of the people of the region,” Poojary said, demanding an apology and questioning the silence of local BJP legislators.
On development, Poojary welcomed the cabinet meeting held in Mangaluru under chief minister DK Shivakumar, claiming that infrastructure projects worth Rs 16,000 crore had been approved for the district. He also highlighted measures allowing local panchayat development officers (PDOs) to issue 9/11 certificates for sites below 1,000sqmt and the proposed addition of 400 beds at wenlock district hospital.
Criticising the centre over tax devolution, Poojary claimed Karnataka receives only 16 paise for every rupee contributed in taxes and questioned BJP MPs from the state over the issue.
MLC Ivan D’Souza, former deputy mayor Purushotham Chitrapura, former corporator Ashok DK, Keshav Maroli, Yogish Kumar, Kiran Budle, K Ashraf, Satish Kandal, Hemanth Garodi and Shamsuddin Bunder were present.

briefs.headline: Residents turn homes into art hubs; Bengaluru community bonds deepen
briefs.bodyText:
Jasmine garlands and candles softened the dimly lit hall at Adarsh Palm Retreat (APR). Guests in ethnic wear left their footwear outside and were welcomed with haldi-kumkum as they settled into the low seating for a baithak-style musical evening. Reality show finalist Koyel Mukherjee sang soulful songs and ghazals, drawing the 135-member audience into the per formance. Many sang along.
Across Bengaluru, some residents are bringing music and theatre into homes and apartment communities. For them, smaller performances offer a chance to pause, meet neighbours and enjoy art close to home. “These intimate musical events recreate the nostalgia of community terrace gatherings during power cuts while offering an alternative to compulsive phone scrolling,” says an APR resident.
Resident Kiran Harjani, who attended with family and friends, said the music revived childhood memories of humming songs with her father. “My favourite was the Sufi song ‘Dama Dum Mast Qalandar’,” she says.
Kiran Grover Adlakha, co-founder of Marasim Entertainment, who is also a resident of APR, says music will remain central to their next few events, with theatre potentially added later.
Adlakha and her friends now plan to replicate the model in apartment communities such as Prestige Lakeside Habitat, Prestige Shantiniketan, and Sobha Meadows.“The 
idea is to bring intimate music or art experiences closer to people in residential communities, right in their backyard, to reduce travel, avoid big crowds, and create a sense of belonging,” says Adlakha, who works with Apple.
Musician Manasi Prasad notes that in big concerts, lighting and distance can sometimes make the audience feel anonymous and hence home performances are more fulfilling.
‘Art In The Living Room’
Vatsala Shrivastava invites known artists to perform for 40-60 people at her home in Purva Seasons in CV Raman Nagar, aiming to bring art to her community and recreate the ‘art in the living room’ ecosystem. She provides the venue, arranges tea and snacks, but neither charges nor earns from these events. Attendees pay ticket costs directly to the artist. “The idea is to nurture art and make theatre accessible to people who find travelling to venues difficult,” she says.
The curated artistic events —mainly interactive solo plays and performances — are inspired by her childhood in Patna, where her writer father, who worked with All India Radio, would hold creative discussions in their drawing room.
A narrative architect and communication consultant, she sends out curated invitations rather than opening them to all. She invites people from her apartment community, her children’s school, professional circles, and artist friends. Attendance has consistently been full.
In Nov, she will host a musical evening at her home featuring Anuradha Sivarajan, an artist trained in classical music, who will perform ghazals, Bollywood, folk, classical, Bengali and Western songs.
“Interactive, minimalist productions with small casts work best for home performances, where large casts or props can be overwhelming,” says Shrivastava, an actor herself, who enjoys English and Hindi plays that spark contemporary conversation and reflect lived reality, regardless of language.
Guests typically mingle before and after the performance. Many stay back to talk with the artists and each other, and friendships are often formed through these gatherings.
Coffee & Conversations
What Rashmi Sharma likes the most about home-based theatre performances is that they allow one to mingle with neighbours and other attendees before the show over snacks and coffee, and have “reflective, thought-provoking discussions after the performance”. She emphasises theatre’s ability to make strong statements and leave audiences with ideas to discuss, calling the overall experience “immersive and enriching”.
Sharma, who is from Rishikesh and now an engineering director in Bengaluru, says such community events allow her to watch plays without having to navigate the traffic, while her 11-year-old daughter can play with her friends nearby. Watching a play just a few floors away feels like a dream come true for her.
Some, like Mansee Shah, a Bengaluru-based artist, are making the most of these settings. A curator who previously ran a well-known art space, Shah now builds art communities and performs in small spaces. Her shows are interactive and often use a ‘playback theatre’ format where audience members share real stories that performers immediately reenact.
As a section of residents aims to demystify art and cultivate a sense of belonging among the attendees, Bengaluru’s cultural scene is witnessing a heartwarming shift that’s showcasing a collective longing for authentic social engagement.

briefs.headline: Task force to be set up to tackle Varthur-Gunjur bottlenecks in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Responding to growing public outrage over traffic congestion and deteriorating road conditions on the Varthur-Gunjur stretch (SH-35), Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) chief commissioner Maheshwar Rao conducted an early-morning inspection of the corridor Saturday and directed officials to constitute a multi-agency task force to accelerate pending works.
This comes in the backdrop of multiple reports by 
The Times of India
 highlighting the pathetic state of road infrastructure in the area, which is dotted with apartments occupied by those working in the tech sector. Residents too had hit the streets to protest severe traffic snarls, poor road conditions, and a lack of coordination among multiple agencies executing infrastructure works in the fast-growing corridor.
Rao walked along the stretch from Varthur Kodi to Varthur police station, inspecting ongoing roadworks, bottlenecks and commuter facilities. Following interactions with residents and officials, Rao said one of the key issues affecting progress was the involvement of multiple agencies operating independently on the same stretch. “I’ve asked Bengaluru East City Corporation (BECC) to form a task force to speed up the work.
 Officials from all the departments concerned must coordinate and complete the pending works in a time-bound manner,” Rao told 
TOI
.
He said several utility-related works were still pending, including those involving BWSSB and Bescom, and identified three major bottlenecks that required urgent intervention. “There are works yet to be taken up by BWSSB, while Bescom is currently shifting utility lines. We’ve also identified critical bottlenecks that need to be addressed so traffic movement can improve,” he said.
Lokande Snehal Kumar, additional commissioner of BECC, said the civic body would soon convene a meeting involving all stakeholder agencies. “We’ll be holding a meeting next week. A multi-agency task force will then be constituted to monitor progress and ensure better coordination. Similar mechanisms will also be considered for other major infrastructure projects.”
Motorable roads & dust-free commute top priority
Apart from the long-term road widening works being executed by Karnataka Road Development Corporation Limited, Rao stressed that authorities must immediately focus on improving day-to-day commuting conditions for residents.
Having walked the stretch himself, the chief commissioner said several portions of the road were in poor condition, with damaged pedestrian pathways and large potholes creating difficulties for both motorists and walkers. “I noticed several stretches where pedestrians are forced to walk on damaged surfaces. There are also multiple locations with large potholes. These need to be repaired immediately to ensure smooth and safe movement,” Rao said.
Dust, another major complaint from residents, also came under scrutiny during the inspection. “There are sections where loose jelly stones have been dumped. We’ve instructed officials to take measures to control dust and make the road more commuter-friendly while the main project continues,” he added.
Officials said ongoing pothole-filling works would continue in the coming days to improve driving conditions. “Repair works have already begun from the Varthur Kodi side and KRDCL is carrying out pothole-filling activities. The corporation will extend all necessary support to ensure the works are completed quickly,” Kumar said.
The latest intervention comes amid growing pressure on authorities to expedite works on the Varthur-Gunjur corridor, where residents say years of rapid development have far outpaced infrastructure creation, resulting in chronic congestion, damaged roads and increasing commuter hardship.

briefs.headline: MLA urinates in public in Bengaluru, abuses man for questioning him

briefs.headline: When Bengaluru sleeps, but doesn’t quite rest
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Bengalureans may be getting adequate hours of sleep, but doctors are increasingly seeing people who wake up exhausted, foggy and feeling as though they have barely rested. Doctors in the city say they are seeing 10-15 such cases a week, with the problem particularly noticeable among working professionals and younger people.
The reasons range from late-night screen use and irregular sleep schedules to fragmented sleep, insufficient deep sleep, undiagnosed sleep disorders, and work-related stress and burnout.
Dr Pavan Yadav MV, clinical director and senior consultant – interventional pulmonology & sleep medicine, KIMS Hospitals, Mahadevapura, said patients at his sleep clinic frequently complain that while they get adequate sleep, they do not wake up feeling fresh. “The quantity of sleep may be good, but the quality is often not. Human beings have something called a circadian rhythm. Earlier, our sleep cycle was naturally tuned to the sun. When it got dark, the brain would secrete melatonin and we would naturally fall asleep,” he said.
However, artificial lighting and prolonged exposure to LED screens, televisions, laptops and phones have changed this, he said. “When light falls on the retina, it signals to the brain that it is still daytime, which suppresses melatonin and delays sleep. 
Sleep timings have consequently been pushed back. When I speak to people, many tell me they are going to bed at 1am, 2am or even 3am.”
Dr Kranthi Mohan Chadalavada, consultant neurologist, Kauvery Hospital, Electronics City, said the number of hours spent in bed cannot be equated with sleep quality. “Fragmented sleep, insufficient deep or slow-wave sleep, circadian misalignment, and unrecognised disorders like sleep apnoea or periodic limb movements can all shorten effective restorative sleep even when total hours look adequate,” he said.
Staying up late can particularly affect non-rapid eye movement (REM) sleep, doctors said. Dr Chadalavada explained that deep, slow-wave sleep is concentrated in the initial sleep cycles.
“Delaying sleep onset compresses the first sleep cycles, which is when slow-wave, deep non-REM sleep is most concentrated. This is the stage most tied to physical restoration and next-day alertness,” he said.
Dr Srinivas M, neurologist, Apollo Hospitals, Seshadripuram, said non-REM sleep accounts for around 75-80% of total sleep and is important for physical and neurological restoration. “During non-REM sleep, the body carries out important repair processes. The brain’s glymphatic system also helps clear waste products and toxins from the brain,” he said.
Mind not at ease
For many professionals, the problem continues even after the workday ends. Dr Yadav said people working with teams abroad, those working from home and those worried about job security are often staying connected to work late into the night.
Dr Srinivas added, “Work stress and burnout can affect sleep, particularly when people go to bed thinking about unfinished tasks, targets or work-related responsibilities. The mind may continue planning or thinking about the next day’s work, which can delay sleep initiation.”
According to Dr Chadalavada, chronic stress can increase night-time awakenings and reduce slow-wave sleep, while burnout can lead to rumination and heightened alertness at bedtime.
Doctors also caution that persistent morning fatigue should not always be blamed on a hectic lifestyle. Obstructive sleep apnoea, insomnia, restless legs, circadian rhythm disorders and narcolepsy can all result in non-restorative sleep. “Loud snoring, particularly when it is accompanied by pauses in breathing, can be an important warning sign,” said Dr Srinivas, adding that feeling excessively sleepy while driving, at traffic signals or during meetings should not be ignored.
Dr Yadav said people need to establish a consistent sleep routine and protect their sleeping hours. “For a couple of hours before bedtime, they should avoid things that stimulate the brain — coffee, tea, energy drinks, sweets and alcohol. At least one hour before their bedtime, they should completely stop screen time — no phone, television or laptop.”
He added that the bedroom should be free of television, excessive noise and other disturbances. “If they continuously do this for a week, then they develop a sleep routine. If you want to sleep at 11pm and you do this for a week continuously, it becomes a habit for you.”
Signs you should not ignore
* Loud snoring or pauses in breathing while asleep
* Persistent morning fatigue despite adequate sleep
* Excessive daytime sleepiness or frequent dozing
* Poor concentration, forgetfulness or brain fog
* Feeling sleepy while driving, at traffic signals or during meetings
Ways to ensure better sleep
* Stick to a consistent sleep schedule and aim for 7–8 hours
* Stop screen use at least an hour before bed
* Avoid caffeine, alcohol and stimulants close to bedtime
* Wind down from work several hours before sleep
* Keep the bedroom dark, quiet and free of distractions

stories.headline: Centre orders captive coal power plants to maximise power output on surging demand
stories.deck: The Power Ministry has directed ⁠generators to sell surplus electricity through power exchanges.
stories.bodyText:
The centre has ordered more than 100 captive coal-fired power plants to operate at maximum capacity from October 1 through year-end to meet what it expects will be a rise in electricity demand.
The Ministry of Power’s order, invoked under emergency provisions of the Electricity Act, applies to plants with installed capacity of at least 50 megawatts.
The aim is to meet an “expected rise in electricity demand in the coming months,” showed the order dated September 25 and seen by Reuters.
Nearly 40% of coal-fired plants are operating with critically low fuel stock due to a surge in power demand as the El Niño climate phenomenon raises temperatures more than usual.
The plants primarily serve industrial facilities such as aluminium smelters, steel manufacturers, cement factories and oil refineries.
The Power Ministry has directed generators to sell surplus electricity through power exchanges.
The order covers 112 plants belonging to companies including Vedanta, Tata Steel, Hindalco Industries, JSW Steel, UltraTech Cement , Reliance Industries, Indian Oil, Bharat Aluminium, Hindustan Zinc and Nayara Energy.
The Ministry has ordered plants to report weekly to the Central Electricity Authority detailing generation, captive consumption, power sales, available capacity and coal stocks.
Separately, the Ministry has extended an earlier emergency order requiring Tata Power’s imported coal-fired plant in Mundra, Gujarat, to operate at full capacity until December 31, citing the demand situation.
Section 11 of the Electricity Act allows the government, under extraordinary circumstances, to direct generators to operate power stations in accordance with its instructions.

Logistics operator DHL Express on Saturday (September 26, 2026) announced an 8.9% increase in its shipment charges in India from January 1 next year.
The annual price hike enables the company to adjust for some of the increased costs arising from various factors such as inflationary pressures, currency fluctuations, and industry-specific cost developments.
As an internationally integrated business operating in more than 220 countries and territories, DHL Express is influenced not only by local economic conditions but also by developments across global markets, the company said.
"This annual price adjustment enables us to maintain the high level of service and reliability our customers expect while continuing to strengthen the resilience and adaptability of our global operations," said RS Subramanian, senior vice president for South Asia at DHL Express.
International trade continues to create new opportunities for businesses, while supply chains are becoming increasingly interconnected and complex, he added.
"We remain committed to helping our customers navigate this evolving environment by investing in our global network, digital capabilities, security infrastructure, and sustainable logistics solutions," Subramanian noted.
DHL Express said it adjusts its prices annually to account for inflationary pressures, currency fluctuations, and industry-specific cost developments.
In addition to inflation, the company's cost structure continues to be affected by factors such as energy costs, compliance requirements, and administrative expenses related to evolving customs, regulatory, and security measures introduced by national and international authorities, it said.
Ongoing labour market pressures in many countries also contribute to increased operational costs, according to DHL Express.
